data.hook: A Dolphins fan flying to Vegas had a blunt take on the season opener: 'None.' Now Clelin Ferrell gets a shot at the Raiders who once drafted him fourth overall.
data.name: Dolphins Elevate Clelin Ferrell for Raiders Opener Amid Rebuild
data.summary: The Miami Dolphins called up edge rusher Clelin Ferrell from the practice squad to face the Las Vegas Raiders in their season opener at Allegiant Stadium. The former first-round pick out of Clemson brings 21 career sacks and veteran depth to a young defense, creating a personal revenge storyline against his original team. Entering a full rebuild with new GM Jon-Eric Sullivan, coach Jeff Hafley, and QB Malik Willis, the Dolphins face low expectations—including talk of an 0-17 season—making this a key test for the regime. Kickoff is 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX, with Miami as underdogs.

data.hook: Ryan Fitzpatrick, the former Dolphins quarterback, dropped a stark prediction on his podcast: a Week 1 loss to the Raiders might doom Miami to an unprecedented 0-17 season.
data.name: Ryan Fitzpatrick Predicts Dolphins Could Go 0-17 After Raiders Loss
data.summary: Speaking on the Fitz and Whit podcast with Andrew Whitworth, Fitzpatrick highlighted Miami's tough schedule, massive $182 million dead-cap hit from past stars like Tua Tagovailoa and Tyreek Hill, and a young roster led by new coach Jeff Hafley and quarterback Malik Willis. No NFL team has gone 0-17 since the schedule expanded, with past low points like the 2008 Lions' 0-16. Fans and analysts reacted with a mix of agreement on the rebuild struggles and pushback, noting De’Von Achane as a key bright spot, as all eyes turn to Sunday's matchup in Las Vegas.

data.hook: Herbie Farnworth scooped a loose ball and weaved through defenders in the dying minutes, sparking the Dolphins' epic comeback in Auckland.
data.name: Dolphins Stun Warriors 26-16 in Historic Qualifying Final Win
data.summary: The Dolphins beat the New Zealand Warriors 26-16 in Saturday's qualifying final at Go Media Stadium, securing their first preliminary final spot after just four NRL seasons. Trailing early amid sin-bins and penalties, they rallied with four tries from Selwyn Cobbo, Farnworth (twice), and Jack Bostock, plus Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow's explosive 80-meter burst. The win extends their streak to eight and earns a home preliminary at Suncorp Stadium, leaving them one victory from a grand final.

data.hook: Ashton Jeanty's X-rays showed a clean bill of health, letting the Raiders running back celebrate his return to full practice ahead of Sunday's big game.
data.name: Raiders Get Jeanty Back, Rule Out Bowers for Dolphins Opener
data.summary: Running back Ashton Jeanty is cleared to play after a full week's practice with no injury designation, bringing a spark to the Raiders' backfield against the Miami Dolphins at Allegiant Stadium. Tight end Brock Bowers, however, is out following a recent knee meniscus procedure, prompting coach Klint Kubiak to shift from early optimism to confirming he'll miss Week 1 but return soon. Fans and analysts noted frustration with the coach's initial outlook, while the healthy Dolphins roll into the matchup ready to go.

data.hook: Brutus Buckeye flexed his strength in Austin, powering through push-ups to outshine Texas' mascot on national TV. Ohio State fans loved every rep as GameDay hype built for the big clash.
data.name: Brutus Buckeye Dominates Push-Up Contest on College GameDay
data.summary: During ESPN's College GameDay in Austin, Brutus Buckeye took on the Texas mascot in a push-up contest and came out on top, energizing Buckeye Nation ahead of the top-10 showdown. Fans shared the clip widely, mixing amusement with rivalry chants like 'Beat Texas' and 'Go Bucks,' while the official accounts ramped up the excitement. No. 1 Ohio State faces No. 4 Texas at 7:30 p.m. ET on ABC, following both teams' season-opening wins.

data.hook: Tua Tagovailoa's fresh start with the Falcons hit a wall just days before the season, sidelining him with an oblique injury from practice.
data.name: Tua Tagovailoa Sidelined by Oblique Injury Before Falcons Opener
data.summary: The Falcons ruled out Tua Tagovailoa for Sunday's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers due to the injury, turning to Cooper Rush to start while Michael Penix Jr. recovers from knee surgery. Former NFL coordinator Todd Haley speculated on a podcast that the 28-year-old has quietly retired, citing his late-season play in Miami and self-preservation mindset like Russell Wilson's. Tua's career with the Dolphins featured multiple concussions, hip issues, and other ailments after a promising start, prompting mixed reactions from fans who see either a sad end or more resilience ahead.

data.hook: Miami Hurricanes dominated Florida A&M 77-7, piling up a school-record 856 yards in their home opener. The lopsided win quickly fueled arguments over their early schedule.
data.name: Miami's 77-7 Rout of FAMU Draws Schedule Scrutiny
data.summary: No. 7 Miami set program marks with 856 total yards and 77 points in a blowout shortened by the mercy rule after leading 77-0 late in the third at Hard Rock Stadium. Rival fans from Notre Dame and Florida questioned the Hurricanes' slate, which includes just one ranked foe so far and an FCS money game paying FAMU $760,000 total. Miami backers noted defending champ Indiana's similar $525,000 FCS matchup this weekend, while the team eyes tougher tests like Clemson, Florida State, and Notre Dame ahead.

data.hook: Tua Tagovailoa once opened up about the mental grind of harsh coaching feedback, wishing for an early end to it all. A twisted clip from that moment has fans laughing and piling on now.
data.name: Old Tua Tagovailoa Quote on Coaching Resurfaces with Fan Jokes
data.summary: In a 2024 Dan Le Batard Show appearance, Dolphins QB Tua Tagovailoa contrasted Brian Flores' constant criticism—telling him he sucked and didn't belong—with Mike McDaniel's positive style that rebuilt his confidence. The clip resurfaced after McDaniel's 2025 firing and Tua's move to the Falcons on a prove-it deal, prompting memes and jabs like fans saying they felt the same watching his throws. Some call out the missing context while enjoying the dark humor; others label Tua a crybaby despite McDaniel's role in his best season and big contract.

data.hook: A Falcons radio host stunned listeners by naming Michael Penix Jr. the worst draft pick in NFL history, despite admitting it's not the young quarterback's fault.
data.name: Radio Host Calls Michael Penix Jr. NFL's Worst Draft Pick Ever
data.summary: During a segment on 680 The Fan’s The Locker Room, former Falcons receiver Brian Finneran labeled the eighth overall pick from the 2024 NFL Draft as the league's biggest bust, citing the tough situation behind veteran Kirk Cousins' $180 million deal. Fans pushed back hard online, pointing to bigger flops like JaMarcus Russell and Ryan Leaf, and noting J.J. McCarthy went just two picks later. The backlash highlighted the heated debate over Atlanta's quarterback plans and how local radio takes can spark widespread fan reactions.

data.hook: Glen Powell, the Austin-born actor and Longhorns fan, stepped up as College GameDay's celebrity picker on the LBJ Library lawn, hyping the massive top-five clash.
data.name: No. 1 Ohio State Faces No. 4 Texas in Austin Tonight
data.summary: ESPN's College GameDay broadcast from the University of Texas campus ahead of the 7:30 p.m. ET kickoff at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium, with both undefeated teams coming off blowout Week 1 wins—Ohio State 56-3 over Ball State and Texas 59-7 over Texas State. Fans fired up the rivalry with playful jabs like a sign mocking Ohio State coach Ryan Day for putting ketchup on brisket, a nod to Texas barbecue pride that even GameDay called out as 'No, just no.' Texas coach Steve Sarkisian kept it simple: 'We're talking about a hell of a football game that's gonna get played tonight.' The Longhorns are slight 1.5-point home favorites, airing on ABC.
